MedicalRequest.title: MedicalRequest
MedicalRequest.description: Represents a medical leave request submitted by a student.

id.description: Unique identifier for the medical request.

studentId.description: Reference to the Student who submitted the request. (Relationship: Student 1:N MedicalRequest)

age.description: Age of the student at the time of the request.

dateRequested.description: Date the medical leave was requested.

timeRequested.description: Time the medical leave was requested.

medicalDocuments.description: Array of URIs to the uploaded medical documents.

statusUpdates.description: Array of status updates for the medical request.

doctorVerificationStatus.description: The approval/rejection status from the doctor who is in charge of the document. For example, Approved, Rejected.

directorApprovalStatus.description: The approval/rejection status from the director after the doctor's initial approval. For example, Approved, Rejected.

rejectionReason.description: Reason for rejection, if the request was rejected by the doctor or director.  May be null.

doctorId.description: Reference to the Doctor. (Relationship: Doctor 1:1 DoctorAvailability)

availabilityStatus.description: Availability status of the doctor (e.g., Available, Not Available, Nurse Available, On Leave).

name.description: The full name of the student.

studentId.description: Unique student identifier, used as document ID.

branch.description: The student's branch (e.g., CSE, ECE, AIDS).

enrolledCourses.description: List of courses the student is enrolled in.

courseAbbr.description: The abbreviation of the course (e.g., DSA, PS).

room.description: The room number for the class.

createdBy.description: Identifier for who created the record.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the record was created.

role.description: The user's role (e.g., student, doctor, director, academic_office).

createdAt.description: The date and time the user account was created.

subjectsHandled.description: List of subjects handled by the doctor.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to ensure authorization independence, clarity, and scalability for the CampusOS application, especially focusing on the Digital Medical & Document Approval System (Module 5). Key design considerations include denormalization for authorization, segregation of data based on access needs, and consistent access modeling.

**Authorization Independence and QAPs:**

*   **/users/{userId}/medicalRequests/{medicalRequestId}**: Medical requests are stored as subcollections under each user's document. This ensures that a student can only access their own requests, achieving path-based ownership and simplifies security rules.

*   **/doctors/{doctorId}/availability**: Doctor availability is stored in a separate collection, enabling easy querying and updates to doctor availability.  This ensures that students can see doctor availability in real-time.

**Structural Segregation:**

*   The data is separated based on access requirements:
    *   Student medical requests are stored under `/users/{userId}/medicalRequests/{medicalRequestId}`.
    *   Doctor availability statuses are stored in `/doctors/{doctorId}/availability`.

**Access Modeling:**

*   **Private Data (Student Medical Requests):** Uses path-based ownership `/users/{userId}/medicalRequests/{medicalRequestId}` to ensure students can only access their own requests.

*   **Role-Based Access Control:** The application logic determines roles based on email prefixes and domains (e.g., `doctor.name@iiits.in` for doctors). This allows for role-based access in the UI and application code.

This structure supports QAPs by:

*   Enabling secure `list` operations. For example, a student can securely list only their own medical requests because of the path-based ownership.
*   Providing clear segregation for different roles (student, doctor, director, academic office), which simplifies the implementation of Firestore security rules.
